findings.issue_text: [High/data] themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_lt.properties:101 — The Lithuanian `totpStep1` value was replaced with Italian text ("Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:"). Wrong language for the locale; Lithuanian users will see Italian.

[Medium/data] themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_zh_CN.properties:112 — The `zh_CN` (Simplified Chinese) `totpStep1` was replaced with Traditional Chinese text (手機/應用程式/裝). Wrong script for the locale and inconsistent with the rest of the file, which remains Simplified.

[Medium/bug] js/apps/account-ui/.../messages_en.properties:188 and js/apps/admin-ui/.../messages_en.properties:3138 — The new value uses Java-only `ChoiceFormat` syntax (`{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}`), but these bundles are rendered by the React apps via ICU MessageFormat (`intl-messageformat`), which does not support the `choice` type; the pluralization will not format correctly (and may error) when displayed in the admin/account consoles.

[Medium/bug] misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java (verifySafeHtml) — If the derived English counterpart file does not exist (or the two non-anchored `replaceAll` path rewrites produce a wrong path), the method throws a bare `RuntimeException` instead of a `MojoExecutionException` with a clear message, crashing the build with a cryptic FileNotFoundException rather than reporting a verification finding.

[Medium/test_gap] misc/theme-verifier/src/test/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessagePropertiesTest.java — All new tests are negative cases; there is no test for (a) a translation with allowed HTML (``, `
`, `

`) passing when the English source contains HTML, or (b) the special-cased normalization keys (`error-invalid-multivalued-size` choice stripping, `templateHelp` `CLAIM.`, `optimizeLookupHelp`, the email RTL strip), which are the most fragile paths the message edits in this PR depend on.

[Low/bug] VerifyMessageProperties.java (normalizeValue) — HTML-entity unescaping (`unescapeHtml4`) is applied to the raw value before sanitization, so a translation that legitimately uses entities to display angle brackets (e.g. `<b>`) is turned into real markup and then falsely reported as "Illegal HTML"; there is no way left for a translator to render literal `<...>` text other than the three hardcoded key exceptions.

[Low/bug] VerifyMessageProperties.java (santizeAnchors) — On the first anchor mismatch it `break`s out of the loop, leaving all remaining anchors in the value; those then get stripped by the sanitizer and produce additional confusing "Illegal HTML" messages for the same key. Also, removal uses `value.replaceFirst(...)` of the matched tag text, which removes the first textual occurrence rather than the occurrence actually matched — wrong element can be removed when identical anchors appear multiple times.

[Low/bug] VerifyMessageProperties.java (santizeAnchors) — The message "Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string" contains neither the key nor the file path, so when the verifier scans many properties files the reported failure cannot be located.

[Low/bug] VerifyMessageProperties.java (normalizeValue) — The whitelist is hardcoded to three exact key names; any other existing or future message containing angle-bracket content (e.g. `<Something>` placeholders) or another `{n,choice,...}` pattern will fail the build, requiring a Java code change per key instead of a maintainable, data-driven allowance.

[Low/bug] VerifyMessageProperties.java (verifySafeHtml) — The file is read twice (once via `Files.readString` with UTF-8 semantics for duplicate-key checking, once via `FileInputStream`/`PropertyResourceBundle` with UTF-8-then-ISO-8859-1 fallback semantics); if a file is actually ISO-8859-1-encoded, characters may be decoded inconsistently between the two passes, producing spurious diffs/reports.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] js/apps/account-ui/.../messages_en.properties:188 and js/apps/admin-ui/.../messages_en.properties:3138 — The new value uses Java-only `ChoiceFormat` syntax (`{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}`), but these bundles are rendered by the React apps via ICU MessageFormat (`intl-messageformat`), which does not support the `choice` type; the pluralization will not format correctly (and may error) when displayed in the admin/account consoles.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show the messages changing to use Java MessageFormat-style choice patterns (e.g., `error-invalid-multivalued-size=... {2,choice,...}` in both js/apps/* and themes/* bundles). However, the finding’s core claim—that these specific bundles are rendered in the React admin/account consoles via ICU/`intl-messageformat` (which would not support `choice`)—is not verifiable from the diff. No code in the PR shows how these bundles are formatted at runtime, nor any switch to ICU formatting; the PR even adds logic in `VerifyMessageProperties.normalizeValue` to specially handle `{...,choice,...}` patterns, implying choice syntax is expected/allowed in this codebase.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java (verifySafeHtml) — If the derived English counterpart file does not exist (or the two non-anchored `replaceAll` path rewrites produce a wrong path), the method throws a bare `RuntimeException` instead of a `MojoExecutionException` with a clear message, crashing the build with a cryptic FileNotFoundException rather than reporting a verification finding.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds verifySafeHtml(), which loads the current bundle and also attempts to load an English counterpart via a derived path (englishFile = file.getAbsolutePath().replaceAll(...)). If reading either file fails (including FileNotFoundException when the derived English file doesn't exist), the code catches IOException and throws a bare RuntimeException ("unable to read file ..."). Since verify() only catches IOException from Files.readString() and verify() is declared to throw MojoExecutionException, these RuntimeExceptions will escape and crash execution instead of being reported as verifier messages or a MojoExecutionException, matching the finding.

[Medium/test_gap] misc/theme-verifier/src/test/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessagePropertiesTest.java — All new tests are negative cases; there is no test for (a) a translation with allowed HTML (``, `
`, `

`) passing when the English source contains HTML, or (b) the special-cased normalization keys (`error-invalid-multivalued-size` choice stripping, `templateHelp` `CLAIM.`, `optimizeLookupHelp`, the email RTL strip), which are the most fragile paths the message edits in this PR depend on.

adjudication.rationale:
The diff adds substantial new validation logic in `VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml()` and `normalizeValue()` (special cases for `templateHelp`, `optimizeLookupHelp`, `error-invalid-multivalued-size`/`linkExpirationFormatter...`, and email RTL stripping). However, the added/updated tests in `VerifyMessagePropertiesTest` only assert failure paths (`Illegal HTML`, `Didn't find anchor tag`, duplicate keys) and do not include any positive/acceptance test demonstrating that allowed HTML (`

`, `/`, `
`) passes when the English string contains HTML, nor any tests that cover the special-case normalization branches. This is a specific, diff-grounded test gap rather than a demonstrated functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] VerifyMessageProperties.java (normalizeValue) — HTML-entity unescaping (`unescapeHtml4`) is applied to the raw value before sanitization, so a translation that legitimately uses entities to display angle brackets (e.g. `<b>`) is turned into real markup and then falsely reported as "Illegal HTML"; there is no way left for a translator to render literal `<...>` text other than the three hardcoded key exceptions.

adjudication.rationale: In `VerifyMessageProperties.normalizeValue`, the code explicitly applies `StringEscapeUtils.unescapeHtml4(value)` to the raw translation value before running the OWASP HTML sanitizer. This means an entity-escaped literal like `<b>` becomes real markup `<b>` prior to sanitization. If the corresponding English string does not contain HTML (thus `POLICY_NO_HTML` is used), the sanitizer will strip the tag and the verifier will report a mismatch as "Illegal HTML" even though the translator may have intended to display literal angle brackets. The diff shows no general mechanism to preserve/allow such literal `<...>` rendering besides the few hardcoded key-based normalizations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] VerifyMessageProperties.java (santizeAnchors) — On the first anchor mismatch it `break`s out of the loop, leaving all remaining anchors in the value; those then get stripped by the sanitizer and produce additional confusing "Illegal HTML" messages for the same key. Also, removal uses `value.replaceFirst(...)` of the matched tag text, which removes the first textual occurrence rather than the occurrence actually matched — wrong element can be removed when identical anchors appear multiple times.

adjudication.rationale: In `VerifyMessageProperties.santizeAnchors`, when an anchor tag in the translation doesn't match the next anchor tag in the English string, it adds "Didn't find anchor tag ..." and then `break`s, returning `value` with any remaining ``/`` tags still present. Immediately after, `verifySafeHtml()` sanitizes `value` with a policy that never allows `` (POLICY_SOME_HTML only allows br/p/strong/b), so those leftover anchors will be stripped and will trigger an additional "Illegal HTML" message for the same key. This double-reporting is directly implied by the control flow in the diff. The `replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(...))` also operates from the start of the string rather than at the specific match position, which can make the removal ambiguous when identical anchor tags appear multiple times.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] VerifyMessageProperties.java (santizeAnchors) — The message "Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string" contains neither the key nor the file path, so when the verifier scans many properties files the reported failure cannot be located.

adjudication.rationale: In `VerifyMessageProperties.santizeAnchors`, the only diagnostic emitted on mismatch is `messages.add("Didn't find anchor tag " + matcher.group() + " in original string")`, which indeed contains neither the `key` nor `file` (unlike the earlier "Illegal HTML...for file ... key ..." message). When scanning many properties files, this makes the failure hard to attribute to a specific entry/file, but it does not change verification correctness—only error reporting quality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] VerifyMessageProperties.java (normalizeValue) — The whitelist is hardcoded to three exact key names; any other existing or future message containing angle-bracket content (e.g. `<Something>` placeholders) or another `{n,choice,...}` pattern will fail the build, requiring a Java code change per key instead of a maintainable, data-driven allowance.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds HTML-safety verification in `VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml()` and uses `normalizeValue()` to strip/replace patterns that would otherwise cause sanitizer mismatches. `normalizeValue()` contains special-case allowances only for `templateHelp`, `optimizeLookupHelp`, and for keys matching `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*` or `error-invalid-multivalued-size`. For any other key whose legitimate text includes angle-bracket placeholders like `<Extensions>`/`<NAME>` or choice formats that include `<` (e.g., `1<values`), the sanitizer comparison can flag it as “Illegal HTML” and fail verification, requiring adding another hardcoded exception in Java. This is a maintainability/extendability concern grounded in the current hardcoded key checks, not a directly provable functional defect for the current diff’s keys.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] VerifyMessageProperties.java (verifySafeHtml) — The file is read twice (once via `Files.readString` with UTF-8 semantics for duplicate-key checking, once via `FileInputStream`/`PropertyResourceBundle` with UTF-8-then-ISO-8859-1 fallback semantics); if a file is actually ISO-8859-1-encoded, characters may be decoded inconsistently between the two passes, producing spurious diffs/reports.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `verify()` reads the file once via `Files.readString(file.toPath())` (uses UTF-8 in Java) for `verifyNoDuplicateKeys(contents)`, then `verifySafeHtml()` re-reads via `new PropertyResourceBundle(new FileInputStream(file))`, which per JDK behavior loads `.properties` using ISO-8859-1 semantics. This introduces inconsistent decoding between the two passes and can cause incorrect/false reports (and generally wrong sanitizer comparisons) for non-ASCII content depending on actual file encoding.
